q-212474.name: Question 1
q-212474.worked_solution:
We convert the absolute value inequality into a compound inequality to remove the absolute value. 

The inequality specifies every number $3x+2$ whose distance from zero is less than $7.$ This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
-7<3x+2<7
$$

Now, we can solve the compound inequality using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}-7<3x+2 & <7 \\ -9<3x & <5 \\ -3<x & <\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

q-215469.name: Question 2
q-215469.worked_solution:
First, we isolate the absolute value on the left side of the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\frac{2x+1}{4}|-\frac{3}{2} & \le 1 \\ |\frac{2x+1}{4}| & \le \frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we convert the absolute value inequality into a compound inequality to remove the absolute value. 

The inequality specifies every number $\frac{2x+1}{4}$ whose distance from zero is less than or equal to $\frac{5}{2}.$ This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
\text{ }-\frac{5}{2}\le \frac{2x+1}{4}\le \frac{5}{2}
$$

Now, we can solve the compound inequality using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{2}\le \frac{2x+1}{4} & \le \frac{5}{2} \\ -10\le 2x+1 & \le 10 \\ -11\le 2x & \le 9 \\ -\frac{11}{2}\le x & \le \frac{9}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

q-215488.name: Question 3
q-215488.worked_solution:
First, we isolate the absolute value on the left side of the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{5}+|\frac{1-3x}{5}| & <2 \\ |\frac{1-3x}{5}| & <\frac{7}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we convert the absolute value inequality into a compound inequality to remove the absolute value. 

The inequality specifies every number $\frac{1-3x}{5}$ whose distance from zero is less than $\frac{7}{5}.$ This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
-\frac{7}{5}<\frac{1-3x}{5}<\frac{7}{5}
$$

Now, we can solve the compound inequality using the usual methods. (Remember that whenever we multiply or divide by a negative number, we have to flip the inequality signs.)

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{7}{5}<\frac{1-3x}{5} & <\frac{7}{5} \\ -7<1-3x & <7 \\ -8<-3x & <6 \\ 8>3x & >-6 \\ \frac{8}{3}>x & >-2\end{aligned}
$$

To make the final result easier to read, we will rewrite it so that the smaller number is on the left:

$$
-2<x<\frac{8}{3}
$$

q-215489.name: Question 4
q-215489.worked_solution:
First, we isolate the absolute value on the left side of the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}1+|17-3h| & \le 9 \\ |17-3h| & \le 8\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we convert the absolute value inequality into a compound inequality to remove the absolute value. 

The inequality specifies every number $17-3h$ whose distance from zero is less than or equal to $8.$ This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
-8\le 17-3h\le 8
$$

Now, we can solve the compound inequality using the usual methods. (Remember that whenever we multiply or divide by a negative number, we have to flip the inequality signs.)

$$
\begin{aligned}-8\le 17-3h & \le 8 \\ -25\le -3h & \le -9 \\ 25\ge 3h & \ge 9 \\ \frac{25}{3}\ge h & \ge 3\end{aligned}
$$

To make the final result easier to read, we will rewrite it so that the smaller number is on the left:

$$
3\le h\le \frac{25}{3}
$$

q-29942.name: Question 5
q-29942.worked_solution:
We convert the absolute value inequality into a compound inequality to remove the absolute value. 

The inequality specifies every number $4z+2$ whose distance from zero is greater than $6.$ This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}4z+2 & <-6 & \text{or} &  & 4z+2 & >6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve each inequality using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}4z+2 & <-6 &  &  & 4z+2 & >6 \\ 4z & <-8 &  &  & 4z & >4 \\ z & <-2 &  &  & z & >1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the final solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}z & <-2 & \text{or} &  & z & >1.\end{aligned}
$$

q-29942.html:
Question 5
?

Solve the absolute value inequality |4z+2|>6.

a
 −6<z<2
b
z<−2 or z>4
c
z<1 or z>6
d
 −1<z<1
e
z<−2 or z>1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We convert the absolute value inequality into a compound inequality to remove the absolute value.

The inequality specifies every number 4z+2 whose distance from zero is greater than 6. This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

4z+2<−6or4z+2>6

Now, we can solve each inequality using the usual methods.

4z+2<−64z+2>64z<−84z>4z<−2z>1

Therefore, the final solution is

z<−2orz>1.

q-215707.name: Question 6
q-215707.worked_solution:
We convert the absolute value inequality into a compound inequality to remove the absolute value. 

The inequality specifies every number $\frac{5-9a}{2}$ whose distance from zero is greater than or equal to $7.$ This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5-9a}{2} & \le -7 & \text{or} &  & \frac{5-9a}{2} & \ge 7\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve each inequality using the usual methods. (Remember that whenever we multiply or divide by a negative number, we have to flip the inequality signs.)

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5-9a}{2} & \le -7 &  &  & \frac{5-9a}{2} & \ge 7 \\ 5-9a & \le -14 &  &  & 5-9a & \ge 14 \\ -9a & \le -19 &  &  & -9a & \ge 9 \\ 9a & \ge 19 &  &  & 9a & \le -9 \\ a & \ge \frac{19}{9} &  &  & a & \le -1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the final solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}a & \le -1 & \text{or} &  & a & \ge \frac{19}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-19350.name: Question 7
q-19350.worked_solution:
We convert the absolute value inequality into a compound inequality to remove the absolute value. 

The inequality specifies every number $5x+2$ whose distance from zero is greater than or equal to $1.$ This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+2 & \le -1 & \text{or} &  & 5x+2 & \ge 1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve each inequality using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+2 & \le -1 &  &  & 5x+2 & \ge 1 \\ 5x & \le -3 &  &  & 5x & \ge -1 \\ x & \le -\frac{3}{5} &  &  & x & \ge -\frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the final solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x & \le -\frac{3}{5} & \text{or} &  & x & \ge -\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We convert the absolute value inequality into a compound inequality to remove the absolute value.

The inequality specifies every number 5x+2 whose distance from zero is greater than or equal to 1. This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

5x+2≤−1or5x+2≥1

5x+2≤−15x+2≥15x≤−35x≥−1x≤−35x≥−15

Therefore, the final solution is

x≤−35orx≥−15.

q-29943.name: Question 8
q-29943.worked_solution:
We convert the absolute value inequality into a compound inequality to remove the absolute value. 

The inequality specifies every number $8-2z$ whose distance from zero is greater than $2.$ This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}8-2z & <-2 & \text{or} &  & 8-2z & >2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve each inequality using the usual methods. (Remember that whenever we multiply or divide by a negative number, we have to flip the inequality signs.)

$$
\begin{aligned}8-2z & <-2 &  &  & 8-2z & >2 \\ -2z & <-10 &  &  & -2z & >-6 \\ z & >5 &  &  & z & <3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the final solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}z<3 &  & \text{or} &  & z>5.\end{aligned}
$$

q-29943.html:
Question 8
?

Solve the absolute value inequality |8−2z|>2.

a
 z<−4 or z>−1
b
 z<3 or z>5
c
 z<−2 or z>2
d
z<4 or z>8
e
 z<−8 or z>2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We convert the absolute value inequality into a compound inequality to remove the absolute value.

The inequality specifies every number 8−2z whose distance from zero is greater than 2. This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

8−2z<−2or8−2z>2

Now, we can solve each inequality using the usual methods. (Remember that whenever we multiply or divide by a negative number, we have to flip the inequality signs.)

8−2z<−28−2z>2−2z<−10−2z>−6z>5z<3

Therefore, the final solution is

z<3orz>5.
